reason: Start building rocky planetesimals by letting stone and metal grains stick in gentle collisions.
expectation: I expect a larger rocky aggregate, though further concentration will be needed for gravity to take over.

alternatives.reason: I could start with icy material instead, but chose to follow the rocky branch first.

effect: Rocky pebbles formed, but simple sticking will eventually run into bouncing and fragmentation, so I’ll follow the gas-drag route.
reaction: The growth barrier makes the next stage more interesting.
reason: Gas drag may help concentrate the rocky pebbles toward a dense swarm.
expectation: I expect the pebbles’ motion to change under gas drag; I’m unsure how directly that will concentrate them.

alternatives.reason: I could begin the icy branch, but prefer to continue the rocky one first.

effect: Gas drag changed the pebbles’ orbits, making a pressure maximum a plausible place to concentrate them.
reaction: The distinction between inward drift and concentration is useful.
reason: Continue the rocky branch by gathering the drifting pebbles at the pressure maximum.
expectation: I expect the pebbles to accumulate into a denser swarm, though it may not yet be dense enough for gravity to take over.

alternatives.reason: I could start making icy pebbles, but want to finish the rocky branch first.

effect: The pressure maximum concentrated rocky solids, making the swarm ready for the gravity step.
reaction: It's satisfying to see a way around the sticking barrier.
reason: Use gravity on the dense swarm to advance the rocky planetesimal goal.
expectation: I expect the swarm to collapse into rocky planetesimals, though the result may be an intermediate stage.

alternatives.reason: I could start the icy branch, but prefer to finish the rocky one first.

effect: Gravity turned the concentrated rocky swarm into planetesimals, completing the rocky goal; the icy branch remains.
reaction: The progression from drifting pebbles to gravitational collapse makes sense.
reason: Start the icy planetesimal branch with the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect gentle collisions to form icy aggregates or pebbles, analogous to the rocky branch.

effect: Icy pebbles formed, carrying both rock and volatile material; the pressure maximum is the next available step.
reaction: The parallel with rocky growth is clear, though somewhat repetitive.
reason: Use the only offered combination to concentrate the icy pebbles.
expectation: I expect the pebbles to gather into a denser icy swarm, perhaps ready for gravitational collapse.

effect: The icy pebbles concentrated into a dense swarm, ready for the gravity step.
reaction: The parallel with the rocky swarm is clear, though repetitive.
reason: Use the only offered combination to complete the icy planetesimal goal.
expectation: I expect gravity to collapse the icy swarm into icy planetesimals, as it did with the rocky swarm.

effect: Gravity bound the icy swarm into planetesimals, completing the remaining goal; they are possible water carriers, not the only source of terrestrial hydrogen.
reaction: The result completes the parallel clearly, though it was predictable after the rocky branch.

mostWorthwhile.text: Concentrating drifting rocky pebbles at a pressure maximum was most worthwhile: it showed a way around the sticking and fragmentation barrier before gravity takes over.

leastWorthwhile.text: The icy branch felt repetitive after the rocky branch, particularly its concentration and collapse steps.

surprise.text: The pressure maximum offered a route to gathering solids without requiring every collision to make a larger pebble.

arbitrary.text: No action felt entirely purposeless, although the icy branch moved straight to the pressure maximum without a separate gas-drag action; the result explained that drag was involved.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter to see how the rocky and icy bodies develop, although I hope the branches become less parallel.
